one_liner: Google Ads API is free to call with OAuth 2.0 and has broad coverage plus a vendor-published MCP server. Production access needs a per-Cloud-project access level: Explorer is mostly automated, Basic and Standard need brand verification or review.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 user flow with a Cloud project client ID and secret. A service account workflow is also documented (OTHER). Developer tokens are now optional and ignored by the API servers, and access levels are tied to the Cloud project.
access_notes: Enabling the API gives Test access immediately. Explorer access (2,880 production operations/day) is automated review in most cases. Basic and Standard need brand verification and review, and Standard requires meeting RMF. No API fees.
blocker_notes: Production use at scale needs Basic or Standard access. These require brand verification, and Standard also needs RMF compliance. Test accounts and Explorer access are quick. Webhooks cover lead forms only. The pages describe gRPC endpoints, so the REST label is low confidence.

evidence.quote: The Google Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 to authenticate and authorize requests.
Creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the Google Ads API, and generating OAuth 2.0 credentials is **100% free**.
automated review and approval in most cases, for up to 2,880 operations per day against production accounts
For new Basic and Standard access applications, you must complete [brand verification]
Basic access applications are automated and will be reviewed within minutes after brand verification and submission.

We have published updated versions of [the client libraries](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/client-libs), the [Google Ads MCP server](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server)
Google provides officially supported client libraries that handle authentication, serialization, and communication with the gRPC endpoints.
Use webhook to send data from Google Ads to your CRM system.
